process.sectionTitle: From requirement to App Store release
process.sectionIntro: The same four stages behind 30+ approved submissions.

steps.title: Requirements & Architecture
steps.desc: Work through requirements with the client or product owner, then choose the architecture — MVVM or Clean, module boundaries, and the data layer — before a screen gets built.

steps.title: Feature Delivery in Sprints
steps.desc: Ship features sprint by sprint with dependency injection and testable layers, XCTest coverage on the logic, and code review on every pull request.

steps.title: Profile & Harden
steps.desc: Profile with Instruments for memory, launch time and responsiveness; fix retain cycles and main-thread stalls; verify against real devices and older OS versions.

steps.title: Release & App Review
steps.desc: Automate builds and TestFlight distribution with Fastlane, prepare App Store Connect metadata, then handle submission, review responses and post-launch monitoring.

items.a: Swift and SwiftUI for new work, UIKit and Objective-C for the large existing codebases I maintain, with MVVM or Clean Architecture, dependency injection and Swift Concurrency (async/await) underneath. CoreData, SQLite and Keychain on the data side; REST and GraphQL over URLSession or Alamofire on the network side.

Yes — ARKit and SceneKit for 3D visualisation and product AR, plus CoreML and Vision for on-device intelligence. I maintain two open-source AR projects: MIARKitExamples, a set of ARKit/SceneKit reference samples, and ARCarRims, a 3D car-rim visualiser.

items.q: Can you deliver cross-platform, or native only?
items.a: Both. Native iOS is where my depth is, and I've also delivered two production Flutter applications in Dart — including CollabCRM, a business operating system covering CRM, project management, recruitment, invoicing and payroll. So I can advise honestly on when a shared codebase pays off and when it costs more than it saves.

items.q: Do you handle App Store submission yourself?
items.a: Yes. I run Fastlane-driven build and release pipelines, manage App Store Connect metadata and TestFlight distribution, and handle App Review end to end. 30+ applications have gone through that process without a compliance rejection standing.

items.q: Have you led or mentored a team?
items.a: Yes — I conduct code reviews and mentor junior iOS developers at MindInventory, keeping architecture consistent and best practices enforced across the team, and I work day to day in Agile/Scrum with sprint planning and CI/CD-driven releases.

I'm serving notice through October 2026 and open to conversations now for work starting from then — freelance projects, contract engagements, or a full-time role. Based in Ahmedabad, and I work with clients remotely across time zones.

Not under my own name — this is my first move to taking clients directly, and I'd rather say so than pretend otherwise. What I do have is eight years of client delivery at MindInventory, an agency, building for international clients to their requirements, deadlines and App Store accounts. The work is the same; the invoice is the only part that changes.
